author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Camp Braveheart is marking its 20th year of bringing children from Massachusetts and Rhode Island together for support after the death of a loved one. The HopeHealth program combines camp activities with conversations and practical strategies for living with grief.

NBC 10 highlighted longtime volunteer Harry Potter, a retired Rhode Island educator and former principal of Providence’s Hope High School. Potter has spent much of the program’s two decades greeting campers, building trust and helping children become comfortable enough to talk about difficult losses.

The camp uses art, music and group activities to help participants express feelings and develop a personal set of coping tools. Organizers say the shared setting can reduce isolation by showing children that other young people are navigating similar experiences.

Although the report focused on one volunteer, the milestone also reflects the work of the broader HopeHealth team and the families who return to the program. Camp Braveheart serves both sides of the state line, making it a regional resource for young people whose grief may not be visible in school or everyday routines.
dek: The HopeHealth program brings children from Massachusetts and Rhode Island together for activities, counseling and practical coping strategies after a death.
headline: Camp Braveheart marks 20 years helping grieving children
